Introduction

This document outlines the minor maintenance 
 procedures P1, 
 which must be performed on an annually bases as indicated by
 Y1 in the above 
 title block

Safety Precautions

items:
A work 
 permit must be issued.
The maintenance staff should be trained, qualified, and carry the suitable ID safety category.

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the 
 work area is required.

Wear your safety helmet, safety shoes,
 breathing mask, safety glasses ... etc.
Generator must be shut downed and isolated

sections.text: Tools and Equipment

items:
Safety helmet, safety shoes, 
 breathing mask, safety glasses ... etc.
Blower, Brushes.

Cleaning
 fluids as Freon - TF, Chlorothene.

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

items: Primary visual inspections.
Clean all surfaces using brushes and air dry compressor.

Clean the all surfaces by using cleaning fluids such as Freon - TF, 
 chlorothene.
Paint the all surfaces of the core if it needed.

Inspect the ends of the stator and rotor winding for deposits of oil and 
 evidence of corona discharge
Inspect the winding and insulation core fully.
Measure stator & rotor insulation resistance. see figure 1, 2
Check LV & DC distribution panels.

Check SFC/SEE cubicles, cleaning, check all alarms for correct functions, 
 cable connections, Thyristors and control cards.
Check auxiliary transformers.
Check bearing insulation resistance.

Check slip rings for exciter current transmission on contamination and damage. 
 Finish turn or grind out of true or non faced slip rings.
Check grounding shaft brushes.
Inspect make up air filter for contamination.
Check generator slip ring brushes.
Check neutral point thermometer temperature.
Check operating air coolers on proper ventilation.
Check condition of slip rings.
Check brush holders.
Check cooling water inlet & outlet pipes.

Check condition of temperature and pressure.
 Measuring devices inside cooler.
Check condition of liquid in generator signal.

Location: Generator 
Designation: Tested by: 
Signature: 
Test Date:

Required Insulation Resistance of Stator 
Winding

New international standards specify an insulation 
resistance of not less than 1 megohm per kilovolt rated generator voltage at at 
40 oC (104 oF)

A correction of the insulation resistance measured 
at the winding temperature prevailing during the measurement to the above 
reference temperature can be made using the diagram in figure 2.

If the insulation resistance measured is lower than 
the specified minimum value, the neutral connections must be separated and the 
insulation resistance of the individual winding phases measured.

During the test, the other two phases which are not 
involved should be grounded. If the insulation resistance of the individual 
phases are likewise lower than the required limit value, drying of the windings 
will be indispensable.

Great differences in the insulation resistance 
values are indicative of local contaminations, e.g. insulators in bus duct or 
terminal bushings. If predicable additional connections should be separated.

If the measure does not result in an improvement, it 
is recommended to obtain the services of a specialist from the manufacture's 
works.
Measurement of Insulation Resistance

Prior to each measurement, the generator must 
 be de-excited and any static charges removed by grounding the windings. 
 The windings should be grounded after each measurement for the duration of 
 the recharging period.

The insulation resistance of the stator is 
 measured between the winding copper and the stator core.

The measurement should be made with a megger 
 giving a scale reading of not less than 1000 mega-ohm. The megger voltage 
 should be not less than 1000 V, but may amount to up to 5000V
Temperature t in oC

Figure 1: Diagram for correction of insulation 
resistance,
measured to a Temperature of 40 oC

Required 
 Insulation Resistance of Rotor Winding

The insulation resistance should amount to > 
1 mega ohm at 40 oC (104 oF)

At winding temperature other than 40 oC, 
correction can be made using the curve shown in Figure 2.

Measurement of Insulation 
Resistance

The insulation resistance should be measured between 
one slipring and the generator shaft, using a insulation resistance meter with a 
voltage < 500V. This voltage will present no danger to any of the devices in the 
excitation circuit.

The duration of the test should be approximately two 
minutes.

After each measurement, the winding capacitance 
should be discharged for not less than two minutes.

The insulation resistance of the entire excitation 
circuit should be measured with the brushes applied. If an insufficient 
insulation resistance value is obtained. all slipring carbon brushes should be 
lifted off and separate measurement conducted on the rotor winding and 
excitation circuit.

Figure 2: Correction of insulation 
resistance, 
measured ( R meas. ) to a temperature of 40 oC
